key_insight: A generalizable, systematic framework for designing and evaluating LLM prompts can produce more pedagogically aligned and personalized follow-up questions in structured educational dialogues. Testing six prompt templates shows how prompt design choices materially affect instructional output quality.
problem_solved: Provides an evidence-based method to evaluate and compare LLM prompts for educational applications, addressing the lack of systematic ways to ensure prompts yield personalized, pedagogically appropriate responses.
method: Design six prompt templates that incorporate pedagogical and personalization elements for generating follow-up questions in a structured dialogue activity.
Apply a mixed-methods evaluation pipeline combining automated metrics and human ratings to assess quality, pedagogical alignment, and personalization of generated outputs.
Compare template performance and surface actionable design principles for prompt selection and iteration in educational settings.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a replicable evaluation workflow to optimize prompts for learning experiences, enabling safer, more effective, and more targeted educational LLM deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart showing: prompt templates → LLM generation → automated metrics → human annotation → comparative analysis
Bar/heatmap comparing the six templates across quality, pedagogical alignment, and personalization
Before-and-after example dialogue: original student turn and alternative follow-up questions from two contrasting templates
Checklist/infographic summarizing recommended prompt design principles
paper_title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
paper_authors: Langdon Holmes, Adam Coscia, Scott Crossley, Joon Suh Choi, Wesley Morris
